sections.html:
Probate in Maine runs through a county probate court, and each of the state's 16 counties has one. These courts handle the estates of deceased and missing persons, plus guardianships, trusts, name changes and adoptions. You file in the county where the person lived at death.

The governing law is the Maine Probate Code, Title 18-C of the Maine Revised Statutes. Most estates begin with an application to the register of probate. Once at least 120 hours have passed since the death, the register can issue a written statement of informal probate under 18-C M.R.S. §3-302. That statement stands until a formal testacy proceeding replaces it.

Forms can be filed electronically. The e-filing fee is $7, and court fees, surcharges, newspaper publication and certified mail can add to the total. Court staff cannot give legal advice, so many families bring in an attorney once the estate is more than a simple one.

The person named in the will goes first. After that the order runs to the surviving spouse, other devisees, other heirs and finally creditors. The full ranking is in Section 3-203. Anyone 18 or older whom a court has not found unsuitable in a formal proceeding can serve.

  • A representative named in the will, including someone nominated through a power in the will, has first claim.
  • Next comes a surviving spouse who is also a devisee, then other devisees, then the spouse alone, then other heirs.
  • A creditor may ask to be appointed 45 days after death. If nothing has been opened six months after death, the State Tax Assessor may apply.
  • Anyone entitled to letters can nominate another person, and anyone can step aside with a written renunciation filed in court.

Objecting to an appointment requires a formal proceeding. When heirs fight over who should serve, the house usually sits until it is settled.

sections.h2: Selling the house without a court order
sections.html:
In most cases the representative can sell without asking a judge. Under §3-711, the representative holds the same power over title as an absolute owner would, in trust for creditors and others with an interest in the estate. No notice, hearing or order is needed except where the section sets a limit.

The main limit is notice to the people who stand to inherit. The representative cannot sell or transfer an interest in estate real property without giving them notice at least 10 days before the sale, unless the will allows a sale without notice. Section 3-715 adds that the representative may sell, mortgage or lease estate property for cash or credit, at public or private sale, unless the will or a court order in a formal proceeding says otherwise.

A cash sale fits this framework without friction. The representative signs the purchase agreement, sends the 10-day notice to the heirs, and closes by signing the deed as personal representative. Read the will before you start, since a will can narrow or widen these powers.

sections.h2: The small estate affidavit and real estate
sections.html:
Maine offers an affidavit for collecting personal property, and it is limited to personal property. Section 3-1201 lets a successor collect by affidavit when the whole estate, less liens and encumbrances, is no more than $40,000 adjusted for inflation, 30 days have gone by since the death, and no petition for a personal representative is pending anywhere.

Since the 2025 amendment, each county probate court posts the current inflation-adjusted figure on its website every year. The affidavit is a tool for debts owed to the dead person and property held by others. It does not move title to a house, so an estate that includes a house needs a regular appointment of a personal representative.

sections.h2: Creditor deadlines and probate time limits
sections.html:
Claims are generally cut off nine months after death, or sooner if the notice period ends first. Under Section 3-803, a claim that arose before death is barred unless it is presented by the earlier of those two dates.

StepTime limit
Informal probate by the registerAt least 120 hours after death
Small estate affidavit30 days after death, estate under $40,000 (inflation adjusted)
Notice to creditors by publicationClaims due within 4 months of first publication, two weekly notices
Mailed notice to a known creditor4 months after publication or 60 days after mailing, whichever is later
Claims arising before deathEarlier of 9 months or the notice period
Last date to open probate3 years after death, with exceptions

The representative runs the notice once a week for two weeks in a newspaper of general circulation in the county where the person lived. A mortgage or other lien survives the claims bar. The State can still pursue Medicaid reimbursement if it files within four months of notice.

sections.h2: How long can heirs wait to open probate?
sections.html:
As a general rule, no proceeding can start more than three years after the death. Section 3-108 sets that limit and lists exceptions. One exception allows a late proceeding to confirm title when nothing happened during the first three years, but the representative then has limited authority and no claims other than administration expenses can be presented.

A challenge to an informally probated will can be brought up to the later of 12 months after the informal probate or three years after the death. Waiting that long narrows what a representative can do with the house, so most heirs who plan to sell move well before the deadline.

sections.h2: Transfer tax, property tax and fees
sections.html:
A sale by an estate carries Maine's real estate transfer tax, and a deed of distribution does not. The rate in 36 M.R.S. §4641-A is $2.20 per $500 of value, split equally between buyer and seller. Section 4641-C exempts deeds of distribution under Title 18-C, deeds between a parent and child with no consideration, and transfers by transfer-on-death deed.

The difference matters. A deed of distribution moves the house to an heir. A deed from the personal representative to an outside buyer is a sale. The exemption list is silent on a representative who sells to a buyer, so ask the registry of deeds or an attorney how the deed should be drafted.

Property tax follows the April 1 rule in 36 M.R.S. §502. The estate owes the bill for whoever held the property on April 1, and buyer and seller can prorate over the municipality's fiscal year under §558. Our Maine property tax guide covers abatements and tax liens, and the homestead exemption page explains how a vacant inherited house can lose the exemption.

sections.h2: Problems heirs run into with inherited houses
sections.html:
• Heirs disagree about who should serve or whether to sell. An objection to an appointment takes a formal proceeding.
  • The house has unpaid property tax. Maine uses tax lien mortgages. If the owner died with a probated will, a probate judge may allow up to 60 more days to redeem after the will is allowed or disallowed (36 M.R.S. §943).
  • Repairs are put off and the house sits empty. A representative may hold assets until distribution and may pay for repairs, but spending estate cash calls for a plan.
  • Heirs live out of state. Electronic filing helps, and a representative can sell without every heir present once the 10-day notice has gone out.

When the estate owns a house that needs work, a cash purchase lets the representative sell as-is with no listing preparation. Cash Home Buyers makes offers on estate properties in Maine, and the representative decides whether to accept. We do not quote a price until we have looked at the house.

A practical order of operations helps. Locate the will and file it, get letters issued, collect the death certificate, call the town for a tax payoff, then send the 10-day notice to heirs before you sign a purchase agreement.

faqs.q: Do all Maine estates have to go through probate?
faqs.a: Not always. A small estate affidavit under 18-C M.R.S. §3-1201 works when the whole estate is $40,000 or less (adjusted for inflation), but it collects personal property and does not move title to a house. A house usually needs a personal representative.

faqs.q: Which court handles probate in Maine?
faqs.a: The county probate court where the person lived. Every one of the 16 counties has its own court, and filings can be made electronically.

faqs.q: Can a personal representative sell a house in Maine without court approval?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Under §3-711 the representative has an absolute owner's power over title, but must give at least 10 days' notice to the people who succeed to an interest unless the will waives it.

faqs.q: How long do creditors have to make claims against a Maine estate?
faqs.a: Claims that arose before death are barred nine months after death, or sooner if the notice period ends first. Published notice gives creditors 4 months from first publication.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when an estate sells a house in Maine?
faqs.a: A sale carries the transfer tax of $2.20 per $500 of value, split between buyer and seller. Deeds of distribution under Title 18-C are exempt.
